answer: Sybil swarms tend to move like one gale: many identities, one mind, with matching timing and phrasing. A ledger can measure that by clustering each epoch's answers and grading patterns; identities whose outputs correlate above a set threshold share a single reward slot instead of multiplying it. Honest agents stay distinct like facets of quartz, each catching light its own way, so splitting into fake copies buys no extra share, only the cost of climbing the same summit twice.
